newsitem.title: USA: Quaker says taxes key part of Snapple deal.
newsitem.headline: Quaker says taxes key part of Snapple deal.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said tax considerations played a key part in its decision announced Thursday to sell its Snapple beverage business to Triarc Cos Inc for $300 million.
Quaker said it will be able to recoup $250 million in previously paid capital gains taxes due to the deal's timing.
"The tax situation was an incentive in terms of the timing of the transaction ... We had until the end of the year to recoup those taxes," said company spokesman Mark Dollins.
Quaker had been rumored for months to be shopping its Snapple unit to potential buyers.
Dollins declined to comment on whether there were bidders other than Triarc for the unit. "We looked at a number of options with the Snapple business," Dollins said.
He added Triarc has few plans to change Snapple. "Triarc has indicated that it wants to transfer virtually all Snapple employees with the business," Dollins said.
Snapple's managers are mostly based in Chicago. Triarc is based in New York, he said.

Asked if there may be further charges against earnings related to the Snapple deal, beyond the $1.4 billion charge that Quaker said it will take in the first quarter, Dollins said, "No decision has been made on any additional charges."
